chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:
I said, 'Regarding the poor person upon whom charity is given, is Zakat al-Fitr obligatory upon him?' He said, 'Yes, he should give from what is given as charity to him.'

key_terms.صَدَقَةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Is a poor person obligated to pay Zakat al-Fitr, and if so, from where should they pay it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a poor person remains obligated to pay Zakat al-Fitr, resolving the juristic debate on whether poverty exempts one from this specific duty. Notably, the Imam specifies that the payment can be drawn from the charity funds (sadaqah) the individual has already received, highlighting the fluidity of wealth status in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the principle that Zakat al-Fitr is a personal obligation tied to the individual's capacity at the time of payment, rather than a static assessment of their overall net worth.
